items.title: UnitedHealthcare Is Dropping Prior Authorization for 1,700 Codes. Only About 120 Apply to Medicare Advantage and Dual-Eligible Plans - 24/7 Wall St.
items.reason: UnitedHealthcare's policy change to drop prior authorization requirements is a significant payer operational policy that directly affects provider claims processing and revenue-cycle workflows, though the enforcement/litigation angle is indirect.
items.summary: UnitedHealthcare announced it is eliminating prior authorization requirements for approximately 1,700 procedure codes, with only about 120 of those codes applying to Medicare Advantage and dual-eligible plans. This policy change reduces administrative burden on providers by removing a key pre-service approval requirement that has long complicated claims processing and reimbursement timelines. The majority of the impacted codes apply to commercial plans rather than government programs, meaning most revenue-cycle teams will see meaningful workflow improvements in claims submission and authorization management. For healthcare organizations, this represents a significant operational change that streamlines the prior-authorization process, potentially accelerating claim adjudication and reducing denials related to authorization gaps.
